$comment: ONE list of cases, run by BOTH sides: the kit's JsonShotLoaderTests (C#) and the hosted shots-lint spec (TS). 'kitErrors' are the loader's exact words; an entry ending in ': ' is a PREFIX (the parser's own message follows and differs by platform). 'shots' is what is loaded, in order. Change the grammar on one side and the other side's run of this file goes red — that is the point (invariant 101).

cases.name: the README's own example loads
a get in setup or in a cheat step is a lever (the fourteenth audit: it runs a property getter, which is code)
every step kind and every condition kind
an empty shots array is an empty catalog, no error
$schemaVersion missing
$schemaVersion 2
$schemaVersion as a string
$schemaVersion as an array 40 deep: shown compact and cut to 64 characters
cases.$why: The eleventh audit: the kit rendered a refused version INDENTED, so its message grew with the square of the depth (an 800,000,056-character error at 20,000). Both sides now show it compact (Newtonsoft's Formatting.None, JSON.stringify) and cut to its first 64 characters.

cases.name: $schemaVersion as a string whose 64th character begins an emoji: the cut stops one short
cases.$why: The eleventh fold: both sides cut a refused version to 64 characters, and neither leaves half of a surrogate pair — the tenth audit's lesson (a lone half is a character the two readers read differently).

cases.name: arrays nested one past the reader's cap, in an ignored field
cases.$why: The eleventh audit: the kit's reader (NovaJson.ParseObject) refuses an array or object inside more than 256 others, the root counted, by name and before anything in the document is read; the site's lint refuses the same document in the same words. A 20,000-deep $schemaVersion cost 1.7 s on every load before it.

cases.name: a huge integer is a number, not a crash
cases.$why: An integer past 2^63 is a BigInteger to a .NET JSON reader and throws when read as a double. The site accepts it, so the kit reads it as a number rather than losing the whole file to the exception. Since the thirteenth audit (M2) a number of seconds is at most 600, so this one is refused by that sentence, which is how the case shows it was read as a number (read as absent, it would have loaded with the default); the case after it keeps a huge integer that loads.
kitErrors: shots[0] ('big').steps[0]: 'seconds' must be at most 600 seconds

cases.name: a huge integer where no rule bounds the number loads (the thirteenth audit)
cases.$why: the huge-integer case above is refused by the ceiling on seconds since the thirteenth audit; a timeScale factor has no bound, so this is still the case that a number past 2^63 is read, and loads, on both sides

cases.name: a name that looks like a date is a name
cases.$why: Newtonsoft turns any date-shaped string into a Date token, which every reader here then sees as 'missing'. Text stays text — a UI element may legitimately be called 2026-09-21T10:00:00Z, and a textContains substring routinely is.

cases.name: conditions nested 8 deep load; 9 deep are refused
cases.$why: A depth ceiling both sides share, checked on ENTERING a condition before anything else is read. Top-level condition = depth 1; each 'all' part is one deeper. The path named is the condition AT depth 9, reported once for that branch.
kitErrors: shots[1] ('deep9').settle.parts[0].parts[0].parts[0].parts[0].parts[0].parts[0].parts[0].parts[0]: conditions are nested more than 8 deep

cases.name: a shot name over 80 characters is refused by its length, without the name (the twelfth audit, M1)
cases.$why: the loader repeated the name in every step's address; the site's cap, 80, is the kit's now, and the refusal does not repeat the name
kitErrors: shots[0]: the shot name is 81 characters long, and this kit takes names of at most 80

cases.name: a shot with more than 500 steps or 500 setup commands is refused by its count, before any step (the thirteenth audit, S1)
cases.$why: the lever cap counts DISTINCT commands, so 16,355 copies of one command froze the editor in one tick; the director yields after each command and step now, and these caps bound how many. Steps are counted first; at both caps the shot loads
kitErrors: shots[0] ('many-steps'): the shot has 501 steps, and this kit takes at most 500
shots[1] ('many-setup'): the shot has 501 setup commands, and this kit takes at most 500
shots[2] ('both-over'): the shot has 501 steps, and this kit takes at most 500

cases.name: a condition with more than 64 parts, counted over its whole tree, is refused at the condition (the thirteenth audit, S2)
cases.$why: one evaluation of a condition runs inside one editor tick and asks the UI about every part (2,255 parts: 1,984 ms on a 3,000-node canvas); nested alls count too (2 + 32 + 32 = 66); 64 loads, flat or nested (2 + 31 + 31)
